$comment: Full cross-system mapping of the canonical NoöPunk skill list (issue #255, deliverable 2/3). Every skill in data/rules/skills.json appears once, mapped into all four families. Each cell is labelled `direct` (the family has a skill/ability of essentially the same scope), `analogy` (a related concept covers part of it, or it maps onto a different mechanic type), or `unsupported` (no counterpart). The point of the labels is that #255 forbids handwaving that the lists are identical -- they are not. Rules never become canonical from this file; it is a comparison gate.

label_vocabulary.direct: Same mechanic type and comparable scope. A conversion is still lossy: numeric scales differ.
label_vocabulary.analogy: Related concept, partial overlap, or a different mechanic type entirely (skill vs move vs aspect).
label_vocabulary.unsupported: No counterpart. The skill would have to be introduced or the fiction resolved without a roll.

families.name: Fate Core / Transhumanity's Fate
families.license: CC BY 3.0 Unported (Fate Core SRD); Transhumanity's Fate is CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 and must not be copied
families.mechanic_type: skills rated as a ladder, rolled against opposition; aspects and stunts carry fictional weight
families.verification: Fate Core's skill list verified against the CC BY 3.0 SRD as recorded in data/sources/game_system_rights.json. Which skills Transhumanity's Fate ADDS (as opposed to inheriting) is INFERRED from its Eclipse Phase lineage, not read from its text, which is NC-licensed and not reproduced here.

families.name: Eclipse Phase 2nd Edition
families.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 -- non-commercial, so text is inspiration only
families.mechanic_type: active skills with a percentile pool, opposed by the same or by a passive value
families.verification: The active-skill names below are INFERRED from the EP2 lineage and the open online reference; the exact list was not re-read from eclipsephase.github.io during this pass. Treat EP2 column names as strong analogies, not quotations.

families.name: Cities Without Number / Stars Without Number
families.license: CWN SRD is CC0; the SWN free edition is free-to-read and NOT automatically an open SRD
families.mechanic_type: short skill list, 2d6 + skill + attribute against a target number
families.verification: The CWN/SWN skill list below is a well-established shared list and was NOT re-verified against the official CC0 SRD during this pass, per #255's warning to verify from the original rather than a mirror. Recorded as the next verification step.

families.name: PbtA / The Veil
families.license: No universal PbtA SRD; Apocalypse World has no CC grant; The Veil is CC BY-SA 3.0 for its text
families.mechanic_type: MOVES, not skills: a trigger, a roll, and a list of outcomes including hard choices
families.verification: Move names below are the generic PbtA idiom, chosen so a reader unfamiliar with narrativist play can see the shape. The Veil's EXACT move list and attribute names were NOT verified against the publisher text; no official SRD is invented here, as #255 requires.

summary.$comment: Computed by tools/issue255_comparison_report.py from the mapping above; never hand-written. A guard fails if these drift.

reading: No family is a drop-in for the NoöPunk list. Fate Core is the closest STRUCTURAL match (skills plus aspects plus stunts) but lacks a psi skill, a leadership skill and a professional skill. EP2 is the closest SCOPE match and is where several NoöPunk skills were originally seeded, but it is NC-licensed and its list is shorter. CWN/SWN is the closest NAMING match and needs three additions (Fray, Free Fall, a psi family). PbtA has no skills at all: every row is a move or a playbook, which is exactly why a PbtA conversion changes the game's type rather than just its numbers.
